idea: Investor relations advisory for UK small caps
buyer: CEOs and CFOs of listed small caps
pain: They do not know how investors actually read them
v1: An investor perception audit for one company
channel: Cold into corporates, warm via brokers
verdict: She knows exactly what investors think, which is the product - but corporates are a cold segment.

why.distribution: Corporate IR is not her network; reaching CEOs requires brokers or cold outreach.
why.demand: IR consultancies are paid for exactly this today.
why.fmf: She has been the investor these companies are trying to reach - genuinely privileged perspective.
why.revenue_structure: Audit then monthly retainer, which renews while the relationship holds.
why.defensibility: Established IR firms have the corporate relationships; her edge is authentic buy-side perspective.
why.tailwind: Flat; small-cap listings are declining in the UK.
why.ceiling: £3k/mo x 6 retained clients = £216k, but six corporate retainers from a cold start is optimistic.

ceiling_arithmetic: £3k/mo x 6 retainers = £216k. Six corporate retainers is reachable in principle but each is a cold multi-month sale. Realistic: 2 = £72k.
carries: An authentically scarce perspective and good retainer economics.
kills: Distribution. Her entire network is on the wrong side of this transaction.
test: Ask two small-cap brokers whether their corporate clients would pay for a buy-side perception audit.
test_fail: Companies already retain an IR firm.
